summary: A common summer resident and intra-African migrant. Grey above, with a broad russet upper breast and banded underparts. The orbital ring, lower mandible and legs are yellow. In flight it looks hawk-like. The male calls Piet-my-vrou, or quid-pro-quo. The female calls pik-pik-pik-pik. It parasitises mostly robins. Months were left unset. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: African Cuckoo has a pale grey throat and breast. Red-chested Cuckoo has a broad russet upper breast.
Black Cuckoo is entirely black. Red-chested Cuckoo is grey above with a russet breast and banded underparts.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^13=8192 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 4096–16384.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

underparts.pattern: Broad russet upper breast, also described as brick-red. Banded below.

viewNotes.note: Grey upper parts and a broad russet breast, banded below that.
Russet upper breast, yellow orbital ring and a yellow lower mandible.
In flight it looks hawk-like. A separate wing pattern was not named.
Russet breast and banded underparts. The underside of the wing was not named.

calls.description: Piet-my-vrou, or quid-pro-quo, loud and often repeated, from a high tree and often in flight. The female calls pik-pik-pik-pik, which was not given a separate file. Grade A from Nylstroom, Limpopo. The filename is rc-cuckoo. The catalogue types it as song.

research.note: Newman calls it a common summer resident and an intra-Africa migrant, without naming months. Status is summer-migrant and monthsPresent was left unset. The bill colour was left empty because only the lower mandible is described as yellow. Population figures were left unchanged.
